desc:
A Squarespace site audit with a fix list shows you what is holding your site back and what to repair first. Ecom Swift LLC reviews your pages for design, mobile layout, speed, SEO, forms and checkout, then hands you a ranked report you can act on.

## What is a Squarespace site audit?

A Squarespace site audit is a structured review of your live site that ends in a written list of problems, each with a clear fix and a priority. It looks at the same things a visitor and a search engine notice: layout, loading time, page titles, working forms and a checkout that completes. The result is a plan, not a pile of observations.

Most owners build a site once and then keep adding to it. Pages drift out of style, photos grow heavy, old blog posts keep outdated titles and a form quietly stops sending emails. An audit finds these small leaks before they cost you enquiries.

## Why a review pays off before you spend on changes

Without an audit, money often goes to the wrong place. An owner redesigns the home page when the real problem is a contact form that lands in a spam folder. Another pays for new photography while the existing images load so slowly that phone visitors leave first.

A prioritized list changes the order of work. You fix what blocks enquiries and sales first, then move to polish. Because each point comes with a plain fix, you can do it yourself, give it to a freelancer or ask us to apply it later.

## What a thorough Squarespace review includes

- Page-by-page notes on layout, spacing and consistency of fonts and buttons.
- Mobile checks of the Fluid Engine layout, including text that wraps badly and buttons that are hard to tap.
- Image weight review, so oversized photos and heavy blocks are named.
- SEO basics: page titles, descriptions, heading order, URL slugs and alt text.
- Search Console and sitemap status, so you know whether Google can read the site.
- Test submissions of contact forms and newsletter blocks.
- Product pages, cart and checkout walk-through for stores.
- Competitor comparison, where the package covers it.
- A fix list sorted by importance, with one plain action per item.

## How we run the audit

We start with the pages you name, then widen to the rest of the site within the scope of your package. We open each page on desktop and on a phone, test every form with a real entry and read the settings that affect search. Where a store is involved, we add a product to the cart and move through checkout without paying.

You then receive the report as a PDF. The Basic package gives a short list of the most important fixes. Standard adds more pages and a list sorted by priority. Premium adds a deeper review, a competitor comparison and a step-by-step action plan, and the one-to-one call can be added to any package so we can talk through the findings together.

## Do and avoid when preparing for an audit

**Do:**
- Tell us your main goal, such as more enquiries or more orders.
- List the pages that matter most, so we start there.
- Mention anything you already suspect is broken.
- Keep your plan and domain details at hand for questions.

**Avoid:**
- Editing the site heavily while the review is running.
- Hiding known problems, which only delays the fix.
- Treating every finding as equally urgent.
- Deleting pages before we check whether they receive visits.

## Who benefits from an audit

A small business owner who has not looked at the site since launch gets a clear picture of its condition. A photographer or consultant whose enquiries have dried up learns whether the cause is speed, wording or a broken form. A shop owner deciding between a redesign and a few repairs gets an honest view of which one is needed.

An audit is also useful before hiring a designer. A written list lets you brief them precisely and compare quotes fairly.

## How to get started

Send us the site address and a short note about your goal. We never need your password. If we need to look inside the editor, you can invite us as a contributor with the permissions required for the review, and you can remove that access when the work is done. We confirm the scope, run the review and send the report, and you decide which fixes to apply and who applies them.
